## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag should take its default from an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable. The project's cli-flags policy requires this for every new flag because CI sets options through the environment.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect` now skips files whose basename matches any of the patterns and logs each skipped path. The change also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds unit and end-to-end tests.

(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — `--exclude` always defaults to `[]` and ignores `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, so setting that variable excludes nothing. `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` says: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable … because CI sets options through the environment." — CI jobs that set exclusions through the environment will archive the files they meant to skip, without any error. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choosing a delimiter such as commas; note that `action="append"` adds CLI values to a non-empty default instead of replacing it, so decide the intended precedence, then extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing`.
